problem:
$$
[T]_{B|C}=[\begin{aligned}9 & -2 \\ 1 & -3 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}],\,[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4\end{aligned}]
$$

Suppose $B$ and $C$ are bases of the vector spaces $V$ and $W,$ respectively. The matrix $[T]_{B|C}$ of the linear map $T:V\to W$ relative to these bases, and the coordinates of the vector $x\in V$ relative to $B$ are shown above. Find $[T(x)]_{C}.$

activity_context.topic_title: The Matrix of a Linear Map Relative to Two Bases

examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Image of a Vector Under a Linear Map Given the Matrix Relative to Two Bases

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14067114/assets/7d82125089d15dada1be4f8d6669b5e125da921019b3a9d27376353dcf59a090.png)

Suppose $\mathcal{B}$ and $\mathcal{C}$ are bases of the vector spaces $V$ and $W,$ respectively. The matrix $[\mathbf{T}]_{\mathcal{B}|\mathcal{C}}$ of the linear map $\mathbf{T}:V \rightarrow W$ relative to these bases, and the coordinates of the vector $\mathbf{x} \in V$ relative to $\mathcal{B}$ are shown above. Find $[\mathbf{T}(\mathbf{x})]_{\mathcal{C}}.$
examples.worked_solution:
The coordinates of the image of $\mathbf{x}$ under $\mathbf{T}$ relative to the basis $\mathcal{C}$ can be found as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[T(x)]_{C} & =[T]_{B|C}\cdot [x]_{B} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & -2 \\ 3 & 7 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-7 \\ -4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem:
Consider the basis $B={{b}_{1},{b}_{2},{b}_{3}}$ of the vector space $V$ and the basis $C$ of ${R}^{2}$ given by

$$
C={[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 4\end{aligned}]}.
$$

Find the matrix $[T]_{B|C}$ of the map $T:V\to {R}^{2}$ relative to these bases if 

$$
T({b}_{1})=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,T({b}_{2})=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,T({b}_{3})=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3\end{aligned}].
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
Recall that $[T]_{B|C}$ is the matrix whose columns are the coordinates of the vectors $T({b}_{1}),$ $T({b}_{2}),$ and $T({b}_{3})$ relative to the basis $C.$

First, we need to find the coordinates of $T({b}_{i})$ relative to the basis $C$ for each $i=1,2,3.$ We can do this simultaneously by considering the following matrix:

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | & | & | \\ {c}_{1} & {c}_{2} & T({b}_{1}) & T({b}_{2}) & T({b}_{3}) \\ | & | & | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

We reduce the left-hand side to reduced row echelon form using Gaussian elimination:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 3 & -1 & 1 \\ 3 & 4 & 1 & -1 & -3\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-3){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 3 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & -2 & -8 & 2 & -6\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:=(-\frac{1}{2}){R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 3 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 4 & -1 & 3\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+(-2){R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -5 & 1 & -5 \\ 0 & 1 & 4 & -1 & 3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the right-hand side gives the matrix of the linear transformation relative to the bases $B$ and $C:$

$$
[T]_{B|C}=[\begin{aligned}-5 & 1 & -5 \\ 4 & -1 & 3\end{aligned}]
$$
